sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: Volume of a cone with radius 3 and height 4?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: Describe the cross-section formed by a cone cut by a plane parallel to its base.
A solid object has mass 8 g and volume 4 cm³. Find its density, and state whether it would float in water (density 1 g/cm³).
A square patio of side 4 m is to be paved at $12 per square metre. Find the total cost, and state which quantity the cost is proportional to.
choices: $192; the cost is proportional to the perimeter
$192; the cost is proportional to the side length
$48; the cost is proportional to the area
$192; the cost is proportional to the area

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 8 and height 2. Leave π in the answer where it appears.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Describe the cross-section formed by a cylinder cut by a plane perpendicular to its base through the axis.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A solid object has mass 91 g and volume 7 cm³. Find its density, and state whether it would float in water (density 1 g/cm³).
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
